transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hello, Doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me, I really appreciate you taking the time. I, um... well, I hope I'm explaining this the right way, I don't want to sound unreasonable or anything. 

I'm mostly here because of some... stress at work. I work in mathematical sciences, specifically environmental modeling. Lately, I've been having this issue where... well, I'm pretty sure the people on our new modeling contract have been tracking my revisions. It seems like they are going in and actually planting errors in the datasets, just to make it look like I'm incompetent and can't lead the work anymore. 

I know how that sounds, and I really don't want to come across as difficult. My wife and the junior analysts at the office, they keep telling me it’s just normal version-control mistakes. Just system glitches, you know? And I try to listen to them, I really do, but... it just feels so deliberate. Does that make sense? I just wanted to talk to someone to make sure I'm handling it appropriately.
Do you think these people are targeting you specifically?

Well, I... I hate to say yes, because I know it sounds a little paranoid, and I really try to be a team player. But, yes, it does feel like it's just me they're focused on. 

I mean, I've been doing this a long time, and I know my way around these models. But suddenly, my specific revisions are the ones ending up with these glaring errors. It’s like they're watching what I do and going in behind me to mess with the data. I don't want to think badly of anyone, and I try so hard to just accept it when my wife or the junior guys say it's just a version-control glitch... but it just seems so targeted at me, to make me look like I can't handle the leadership role anymore. 

I hope I'm not coming across as too accusatory. I just want to do my job well, you know? Does it seem unreasonable for me to feel this way?
Do you think anyone else is involved in this supposed plot against you?

Oh, no, no. I... I definitely don't think it's anything like a big, elaborate conspiracy. I really don't want you to think I'm... well, making mountains out of molehills or losing my grip or anything. 

It's really just those specific individuals on the new contract. Everyone else at the office has been perfectly fine, and I try my very best to maintain good relationships with all the other teams. I'm not trying to point fingers at the whole world, I promise. I just... I just want to figure out how to handle this one isolated issue with the datasets without causing any unnecessary trouble for the company. 

Does that seem like a reasonable way to look at it? I really hope I'm not sounding too difficult or dramatic.
Do you think these individuals are trying to harm you in any way beyond just your work?

Oh, no, definitely not. I... I really want to be clear about that, because I know how this must all sound. I don't think they're trying to hurt me physically or... or ruin my personal life or anything like that. 

I just... I really think it's just about the work. Like I mentioned, it's just that they're tracking my revisions and planting those errors in the datasets. I think they just want to make it look like I can't lead the project anymore. And I know my wife and the junior analysts keep telling me it's just version-control mistakes, and I really, really try to see it their way so I don't cause a fuss. I don't want to be a problem for anyone. 

It's just... it's just the environmental modeling contract, and my role there. That's all it is, I promise. I hope that makes sense? I just want to make sure I'm keeping things in perspective.
Have you ever considered the possibility that these errors might be due to your own mistakes rather than someone intentionally trying to sabotage you?

I... well, I mean, I certainly try to be open to that. I really do. I know I'm not perfect, and I've always been the first to admit when I make a mistake. I don't want you to think I'm someone who just blames others when things go wrong. 

But... it's just that I've been doing this for so long, you know? I know the math, I know the models. And the errors... they're just so specific. They only show up right after I've finalized my revisions on the datasets for this environmental modeling contract. It's like someone is tracking exactly what I do and planting them there. 

I know my wife and the junior analysts keep telling me it's just version-control mistakes, and I try so hard to believe them because I really don't want to cause any trouble or seem difficult. I hate even thinking this way. But it just feels so clear that they're doing it to make it look like I can't lead the work anymore. 

I hope you don't think I'm just being stubborn or refusing to take responsibility. Does it make sense why I'd feel this way, given how the errors are happening?
Do you think these errors could be happening without anyone intentionally causing them, or do you believe that's impossible?

I... well, I don't want to say anything is impossible. I really don't want to sound like I'm completely closed off to reason, or... or like I'm just being paranoid. I try very hard to listen to the junior analysts and my wife when they say it's just version-control mistakes. I really do. 

But... it's just so hard to accept that it's just an accident. The way the errors appear, right after my revisions... it just feels so intentional. Like they are tracking what I do and planting them there specifically to make me look incompetent so I can't lead the work anymore. 

I know that sounds... well, I know how it sounds. And I really, really wish I could just brush it off as a computer glitch or a mistake on my end. I don't want to be the guy who thinks people are out to get him. I just... I can't shake the feeling that they're doing this on purpose. 

I'm sorry, I hope I'm not being too difficult. Does that make sense, why I'm having such a hard time believing it's just an accident?
Do you still believe that people are intentionally sabotaging your work at this moment?

I... yes, I do. I mean, I try not to, but... yes. I really am pretty sure they're doing it right now. The people on the environmental modeling contract, I mean. 

I know we've been talking in circles about this, and I really don't want to frustrate you. I know my wife and the junior analysts keep telling me it's just version-control mistakes, and I swear to you, I try to listen to them. I try to be reasonable. But I just can't get past the feeling that they're tracking my revisions and planting those errors in the datasets to make it look like I can't lead the work. 

I'm sorry, I know that's not what anyone wants to hear. I know it makes me sound... well, you know. I just want to be honest with you because I want to get this sorted out. Is it okay that I'm still feeling this way? I'm really trying my best here.
Have you been feeling sad or empty most of the time lately?

I... no, no, not really sad or empty. I mean, sure, I get a little stressed sometimes with all the contract stuff and the errors, but I'm generally a pretty positive guy. I try to keep my chin up, you know? 

I really don't want you to think I'm depressed or anything like that. I still enjoy things, and I try to be good company for my wife. I'm not sitting around feeling sorry for myself, I promise. I just... I just want to figure out this work situation. 

Does that sound alright? I hope I'm giving you the right kind of answers. I really am doing okay emotionally, mostly.
Do you think your belief about people sabotaging your work could be wrong?

I... well, I suppose anything is possible, right? I really want to be the kind of person who can admit when they're wrong. I try to be open-minded. When my wife and the junior analysts tell me it's just version-control mistakes, I nod and I agree with them because I want them to be right. I really do. 

But... when I sit down and look at the datasets, and I see those errors popping up exactly where I just made my revisions... it's just so hard to see it as anything else. It really does feel like the people on that environmental modeling contract are tracking what I do and planting those errors to make me look like I can't lead the work. 

I know I've said that a few times now, and I really don't want to sound like a broken record or... or like I'm being stubborn. I'm trying so hard to look at it logically. It's just... the evidence feels so clear to me, even when I try to talk myself out of it. 

I hope you don't think I'm just being completely unreasonable. I am trying to see their side of it, I promise. Does that make sense? That I want to be wrong, but I just can't quite get there?
Do you think your belief about people sabotaging your work is based on facts or just a feeling you have?

I... well, I really want to say it's just a feeling. I know that's what a reasonable person would say, right? And I really try to be reasonable. I don't want to come across as someone who jumps to wild conclusions. 

But... when I'm looking right at the screen, it feels like facts to me. I mean, I make a revision, and then suddenly there's an error planted right there in the dataset. It's so specific. It really seems like the people on the environmental modeling contract are tracking exactly what I do to make it look like I can't handle leading the work. 

I know my wife and the junior analysts say the facts point to version-control mistakes, and I swear, I try to agree with them. I don't want to be difficult. I just... I see the errors right after I work on the files, and it's hard to ignore that. 

I'm sorry if that's not the right answer. I know I should probably just accept what everyone else is saying. Am I making things too complicated by focusing on this? I really do want to be cooperative.
Do you think your belief about people sabotaging your work could be a mistaken idea that is not based in reality?

I... I know you're asking me that because... well, because it probably sounds like I've lost touch with reality, doesn't it? I really don't want you to think that about me. I want to be the kind of patient who just says, "Yes, Doc, you're right, it's all in my head." 

I know I keep bringing up the same things... about the people on that environmental modeling contract. I know I've told you how I'm pretty sure they’ve been tracking my revisions and planting those errors in the datasets. And I know I told you my wife and the junior analysts keep telling me it’s just version-control mistakes. I really do listen to them. I hate that I can't just agree with them and make everyone's lives easier. 

But... it's just so hard to say it's not based in reality when I see it happening. It really does feel like they are doing it on purpose to make it look like I can’t lead the work. If I didn't feel so strongly that it was really happening, I wouldn't keep bringing it up, I promise. 

I hope I'm not frustrating you by giving you the same answers. I'm really trying to be helpful and honest with you. Do you think we can still work through this, even if I'm having a hard time letting that idea go? I really want to do whatever is best.
Have you had this belief about people sabotaging your work for a long time, or is it something that started recently?

I... well, I hope it helps that it hasn't been going on forever. I really want to give you a good answer here, and I hope this is a good sign. It’s relatively recent, I think. 

I'd say... it’s been about the last two months. That’s when this... this certainty really settled in, that the people on the project are tracking my revisions and planting those errors. Before that, everything was fine, I promise. I was just doing my math, working with the data, getting along with everyone just fine. 

So, two months... that's not too terribly long, is it? I'm hoping since it hasn't been years and years, it means I'm not entirely a lost cause. I really do want to get back to being a good team player and not causing a fuss for the junior analysts or my wife. I don't want to be a burden to anyone. 

Does that timeframe make sense to you? I'm hoping that since it just started a couple of months ago, it might be easier for us to fix.
Have you ever had a period of time where you didn't believe people were sabotaging your work at all since this started two months ago?

I... well, I really want to say yes. I know it would probably sound much better if I could tell you that I've had days where I just completely brushed it off and didn't think about it at all. I really try to be objective, I do. 

But... if I'm being completely honest, and I know I need to be honest with you... no, I haven't really had a break from it. Since it started about two months ago, it's just... it's always there in the back of my mind whenever I'm looking at the data. Even when I try to tell myself it's just a version-control issue like my wife says, the feeling that they're doing it on purpose just doesn't go away. 

I'm sorry, I know that's probably not the answer you were hoping for. I feel bad that I can't just shake it off. Does that make things much worse? I really am trying my best to work with you on this.
Have you been experiencing any feelings of guilt or worthlessness lately?

I... well, I wouldn't say I feel worthless. I really try to stay positive, you know? I know how important it is to keep a good attitude, especially when things are stressful. I still go to work, I still do my math, I still try to be a good husband. I really do have a lot to be thankful for. 

As for guilt... I mean, I guess I feel a little bad sometimes that I keep bothering my wife and the junior analysts with all this. I know it's probably annoying for them to keep hearing about the datasets and the revisions. I hate feeling like I'm causing trouble or making extra work for people when they're just trying to do their jobs. 

But it's not like a deep, terrible guilt, or feeling like I'm a bad person or anything like that. Just... you know, the normal amount of feeling bad when you know you're being a bit of a handful. 

I hope that's okay to say. I really am trying not to be a burden on anyone. Does that sound like a normal way to feel about all this?
Do you still think that people on the environmental modeling contract are sabotaging your work?

I... well, yes. I really wish I could tell you that I've let it go, because I know that's probably what you'd like to hear, and I really do want to be cooperative. I try to listen when my wife or the junior analysts tell me it's just a version-control mistake. I really try to be open-minded about it.

But... yes, deep down, I'm still pretty sure they're tracking my revisions and planting those errors in the datasets. It just feels like they want to make it look like I can't lead the work anymore. I'm sorry, I know it probably sounds unreasonable, and I hate to be stubborn about it. I just can't seem to shake the feeling that it's deliberate. 

I hope you're not disappointed in me for still thinking that way. I'm really trying to be honest with you so we can figure this out together. Is it... is it okay that I still feel that way, even though I'm trying not to?
Do you think your belief about people sabotaging your work could be a delusion?

I... I know that's the word people use. And I really, really want to agree with you, because I know you're the expert here and I want to do this right. I've tried so hard to look at it the way my wife and the junior analysts do, when they tell me it's just version-control mistakes. I really try to be reasonable and see it from their perspective. 

But... I'm sorry, I just can't quite see it as a delusion. I'm still pretty sure the people on that environmental modeling contract have been tracking my revisions and planting those errors in the datasets to make it look like I can't lead the work. I know that's exactly why I'm here talking to you, and I feel awful that I can't just give you the answer you're probably looking for. 

I'm really not trying to be difficult or dismiss your expertise. I just... I can't turn off how real it is to me. I'm sorry. Is it okay that I'm just being honest with you about that? I really hope I'm not frustrating you.
Do you think it's possible that your belief about people sabotaging your work is something that only you believe and isn't based on real events?

I... I really want to say yes, because I know that would probably be the right answer, and I really do want to agree with you. And you make a very fair point about me being the only one. I know my wife and the junior analysts don't believe it's happening. They keep telling me it's just normal version-control mistakes, and I promise you, I try so hard to just accept that and move on. 

But... when I'm actually looking at the work, I just... I'm still so sure that the people on that environmental modeling contract have been tracking my revisions and planting those errors in the datasets. It just feels too specific, like they're trying to make it look like I can't lead the work anymore. 

I know it's just me who sees it that way, and I feel terrible that I can't just let it go and agree that it isn't real. I really wish I could, just to make things easier for everyone, including you. I'm sorry, I know I probably sound like a broken record, and I really don't want to be a difficult patient. I hope you can understand why it's so hard for me to just dismiss it... am I doing okay explaining all this? I really hope I'm not testing your patience.
Do you still believe that people are sabotaging your work at this moment?

I... oh, I know we've been going around in circles about this, and I really, really wish I could give you a different answer right now. I want to tell you that the feeling is gone, because I know that would mean I'm making progress, and I want to be a good patient for you, I really do. 

But... yes, even right at this very moment, sitting here with you... I still believe it. I know my wife keeps trying to reassure me, and the junior analysts swear it's just a version-control mistake. And I promise I try so hard to agree with them and just let it be. 

But deep down, I'm just... I'm still pretty sure those people on the environmental modeling contract are tracking my revisions and putting those errors in the datasets. It still feels like they're trying to prove I can't lead the work. 

I'm so sorry. I know I keep saying the exact same thing to you, and I feel awful that I can't just snap out of it and give you the right answer. I hope you're not giving up on me... am I still doing okay? I really want to make sure I'm not making you too frustrated with me.
Do you think your belief that people are sabotaging your work could be false?

I... I really, really want to say yes. I know you're asking because you want me to see it that way, and I want to be cooperative. I know I should just accept it when my wife and the junior analysts say it's just normal version-control mistakes. I really try to be open to the idea that I could just be wrong about the whole thing.

But... I'm sorry, I just... I can't quite get there. When I look at the datasets, I just can't shake the feeling that it's the people on that environmental modeling contract. I'm still so sure they're tracking my revisions and planting those errors to make me look incompetent. 

I know I'm probably disappointing you by not being able to just admit it could be false. I feel terrible that I can't just give you the answer you want. I really am trying my best to work with you on this. Is it alright that I'm just being honest about how hard it is for me to let go of this? I really hope I'm not being too difficult.
